propositions.text: Four Croatian citizens claim refugee protection under IRPA sections 96 and 97(1).
propositions.quote: XXXX XXXX (hereafter known as the principal claimant), XXXX XXXX, XXXX XXXX and XXXX XXXX, all citizens of Croatia, claim refugee protection pursuant to Sections 96 and 97(1) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act1 (IRPA).

propositions.text: XXXX XXXX was appointed Designated Representative for the minor children.
propositions.quote: XXXX XXXX was appointed the Designated Representative for the minor children.

paragraphs.summary: Four Croatian citizens claim refugee protection under IRPA; XXXX XXXX is Designated Representative for minors, court states.

propositions.text: The claim specifics are in the claimants' Personal Information Forms and amendments; following is a summary.
propositions.quote: The specifics of the claim are set out in the narrative to the claimants Personal Information Forms2 (PIF) and amendments; however the following is a summary.

paragraphs.summary: The claim specifics are in the claimants' Personal Information Forms; court provides a summary.

propositions.text: Claimants allege periodic discrimination and persecution in Croatia due to ethnicity.
propositions.quote: The claimants allege that they have faced periodic discrimination and persecution in Croatia due to their ethnicity.

propositions.text: Principal claimant fears certain individuals targeting him for Croatian Bosnian background and Serbian military involvement.
propositions.quote: The principal claimant (PC) specifically fears certain individuals, and believes that they are targeting him due to his Croatian Bosnian background, and involvement in the Serbian military.

propositions.text: Claimants lived in a small town outside XXXX in Croatia their entire time there.
propositions.quote: The claimants resided in the small town of XXXX, outside of XXXX for their entire time in Croatia.

paragraphs.summary: Claimants allege ethnic discrimination and persecution; PC fears individuals targeting him for background and military involvement; lived in small Croatian town, applicant states.

propositions.text: Claimants faced racial slurs, bullying at school, and workplace discrimination.
propositions.quote: The discrimination that the claimants faced included racial slurs, bullying of their son's in school, and discrimination in the workplace.

propositions.text: Both adults worked until departure; XXXX alleges job discrimination applying as a XXXX.
propositions.quote: Both adult claimants have a long work history in Croatia and worked up until their departure to Canada, though XXXX alleges discrimination in trying to secure a job as a XXXX.

propositions.text: Children remained in school until coming to Canada.
propositions.quote: Their children remained in school until coming to Canada.

paragraphs.summary: Claimants faced racial slurs, bullying, workplace discrimination; adults worked until departure; children in school, applicant states.

propositions.text: PC crossed into Bosnia twice yearly to visit family, last time one month before Canada arrival.
propositions.quote: The PC crossed into Bosnia on average twice a year to visit family in Bosnia, and did so one month prior to coming to Canada.

propositions.text: PC fears two individuals from his town who have not forgotten the war.
propositions.quote: The PC fears two specific individuals from his town whom he states have not forgotten the war.

propositions.text: Problems began in 2005 after PC confronted parents about their children teasing his son for being Serbian.
propositions.quote: His problems with them began in 2005, when he approached them as their children had been teasing his son for being Serbian.

propositions.text: After confrontation, claimants had graffiti on building and children intimidated by one parent.
propositions.quote: Following his discussion with these parents the claimants had graffiti written on their building, and their children were being intimidated by one of the parents.

propositions.text: PC reported these incidents to police.
propositions.quote: The PC reported this to the police.

paragraphs.summary: PC visited Bosnia twice yearly; fears two individuals; problems began after confronting parents about teasing; graffiti and intimidation followed; PC reported to police, applicant states.

propositions.text: In 2011, PC's son was assaulted and robbed by unknown hooligans; police tried to find photos but failed.
propositions.quote: In 2011 his son was assaulted by unknown hooligans and robbed. This was also reported to the police and while the police tried to find photographs matching the description, they could not.

paragraphs.summary: In 2011, PC's son was assaulted and robbed; police investigated but found no photos, applicant states.

propositions.text: Claimants left Croatia after 2011 event and came to Canada in 2011 to file refugee claim.
propositions.quote: The claimants decided to leave Croatia following the XXXX 2011 event, and in XXXX 2011, came to Canada and filed for refugee protection.

paragraphs.summary: Claimants left Croatia after 2011 event and filed refugee claim in Canada, applicant states.

propositions.text: Claimants are neither Convention refugees nor persons in need of protection.
propositions.quote: I find that the claimants are neither Convention refugees nor persons in need of protection.

paragraphs.summary: Court finds claimants are neither Convention refugees nor persons in need of protection.

propositions.text: Determinative issue is state protection in Croatia; claimants failed to establish past persecution and have subjective fear issues.
propositions.quote: The determinative issue in this claim is state protection in Croatia; however significant subjective fear issues arise with the claimants' evidence and they failed to establish past persecution.

paragraphs.summary: Court identifies state protection as key issue; claimants failed to prove past persecution and have subjective fear issues.

propositions.text: Post hearing submissions from counsel were received and considered.
propositions.quote: Counsel's post hearing submissions were received and considered.

paragraphs.summary: Court received and considered counsel's post hearing submissions.

propositions.text: Claimants' Croatian citizenship established by testimony and identity documents including passports.
propositions.quote: The claimants' identities as citizens of Croatia are established by their testimony and by the personal identity documents filed, including their Croatian passports.

paragraphs.summary: Court finds claimants' Croatian citizenship established by testimony and documents.

propositions.text: To be a Convention refugee, claimant must have well-founded fear of future persecution.
propositions.quote: To be found a Convention refugee, a claimant must have a well-founded fear of future persecution.

propositions.text: Distinction exists between persecution and discrimination or harassment; persecution involves more serious mistreatment.
propositions.quote: A distinction can and should be made between persecution, on the one hand, and discrimination or harassment on the other; with persecution being characterized by the greater seriousness of the mistreatment it involves.

propositions.text: Finding of discrimination is within Refugee Protection Division's jurisdiction.
propositions.quote: A finding of discrimination is within the jurisdiction of the Refugee Protection Division.

paragraphs.summary: Court states legal test: well-founded fear needed; persecution differs from discrimination; discrimination findings are within tribunal's jurisdiction.

propositions.text: Cumulative acts of discrimination may constitute persecution in certain circumstances.
propositions.quote: The panel notes that cumulative acts of discrimination might indeed constitute persecution, in certain circumstances.

paragraphs.summary: Court notes cumulative discrimination can amount to persecution in some cases.

propositions.text: UNHCR Handbook states discrimination only amounts to persecution if it causes serious prejudicial consequences.
propositions.quote: The UNHCR Handbook on Procedures and Criteria for Determining Refugee Status notes that: Differences in the treatment of various groups do indeed exist to a greater or lesser extent in many societies. People who receive less favourable treatment as a result of such differences are not necessarily victims of persecution. It is only in certain circumstances that discrimination will amount to persecution. This would be so if measures of discrimination lead to consequences of a seriously prejudicial nature for the person concerned, e.g. serious restrictions on his right to earn his livelihood, his right to practice his religion, or his access to normally available educational facilities.

paragraphs.summary: UNHCR Handbook says discrimination is persecution only if it causes serious prejudicial consequences, court cites.

propositions.text: Objective evidence shows ethnic minorities' situation in Croatia improved over 10 years but some harassment remains.
propositions.quote: Objective evidence indicates that the situation of ethnic minorities in Croatia has improved in the past 10 years, though minorities still face some harassment and discrimination.

propositions.text: Human rights groups report ethnic and religious relations stable with sporadic violence and threats against all religious groups.
propositions.quote: Human rights groups and religious leaders report that overall ethnic and religious relations remain stable, with some noted sporadic violence and threats directed against all religious groups.

paragraphs.summary: Court finds ethnic minorities' situation improved but some harassment remains; relations stable with sporadic violence, per evidence.

propositions.text: Ethnic Serbs are largest minority in Croatia, about 4.5% of population; actual numbers likely higher due to census issues.
propositions.quote: Ethnic Serbs are the largest minority in Croatia, constituting around 4.5 per cent of the population. It is estimated that the numbers are far greater as many Serbs spend long periods of time outside of Croatia and are not present for census taking.

paragraphs.summary: Court states ethnic Serbs are largest minority in Croatia, about 4.5%, likely undercounted.

propositions.text: Some Serbs faced housing discrimination but claimants had consistent housing in XXXX from arrival date.
propositions.quote: There is some evidence that some Serbs have faced discrimination in housing, however these claimants had housing in XXXX, Croatia consistently from the date of their arrival.

propositions.text: No evidence at hearing of housing access restriction for claimants.
propositions.quote: No evidence was provided at the hearing on a restriction of access to housing.

paragraphs.summary: Court finds some Serbs face housing discrimination but claimants had consistent housing; no evidence of housing restriction for claimants.

propositions.text: No persuasive evidence of restriction or denial of education, livelihood, or religious practice for claimants in Croatia.
propositions.quote: Similarly, there is no persuasive evidence of any restriction or denial of an education, opportunity to earn a livelihood or evidence of any restriction on the practice of religion in the short time that these claimants resided in Croatia.

paragraphs.summary: Court finds no persuasive evidence claimants faced education, livelihood, or religious practice restrictions in Croatia.

propositions.text: Children were in school until Canada; bullying alleged but no evidence of restricted educational access.
propositions.quote: The two minor children were in school until relocating to Canada, and while the claimants allege that they experienced periodic bullying, there is no persuasive evidence of any restriction to access an educational facility.

paragraphs.summary: Court finds children attended school until Canada; bullying alleged but no evidence of restricted access.

propositions.text: XXXX alleges discrimination applying for XXXX job due to Serbian ethnicity; no formal complaints filed.
propositions.quote: XXXX alleges that she experienced discrimination in finding employment as a XXXX in Croatia. She indicates that she applied to the only XXXX in her area, and that she was turned down as she is Serbian.

propositions.text: She secured other employment consistently in XXXX from 2001-2011 until departure.
propositions.quote: She did not file any formal complaints about discrimination, and was able to secure other employment consistently in XXXX until departure to Canada, from 2001-2011.

paragraphs.summary: XXXX alleges job discrimination applying for XXXX due to Serbian ethnicity but found other jobs; no complaints filed, applicant states.

propositions.text: Not finding employment in one's chosen field is not persuasive evidence of a substantial restriction on the right to earn a livelihood.
propositions.quote: not finding employment in ones chosen field is not persuasive evidence of a substantial restriction on the right to earn a livelihood

propositions.text: Professionals often redirect careers due to economic changes or new country location.
propositions.quote: It is not uncommon for professionals to have to redirect their careers to adjust to changing economic situations, or to a new country location

propositions.text: Documents confirm Serbs face employment difficulties in some areas, but PC's evidence was not persuasive that ethnicity caused his employment problems.
propositions.quote: While the documents do confirm that in some areas Serbs are subject to difficulties in accessing employment, the PC's evidence was not persuasive that her problems in securing employment were due to ethnicity

paragraphs.summary: The court finds employment difficulties do not prove substantial livelihood restriction; career redirection is common; PC's ethnicity-based employment claim unpersuasive.

propositions.text: Claimants allege harassment by known offenders in their town.
propositions.quote: The claimants allege harassment by known offenders in the town of XXXX

propositions.text: Claimants' choice to remain in the town, delay in leaving, and frequent returns to Croatia undermine their subjective fear and persecution claim.
propositions.quote: I find their choice to remain located in the same small town, their long delay in departure from the start of events, and their frequent reavailments of Croatia severely undermine their subjective fear and the establishment of persecution at all

paragraphs.summary: Claimants allege harassment, but court finds their conduct undermines subjective fear and persecution claim.

propositions.text: Persecution is harm inflicted with repetition or persistence.
propositions.quote: Persecution is defined in refugee law to be the inflicting of harm with repetition or persistence

propositions.text: PC fears a specific individual but did not report to police; evidence of racial slurs and intimidation since 2005.
propositions.quote: The PC fears a specific individual that he chose not to report to the police, and provided evidence of racial slurs and intimidation of his sons and wife dating back to 2005

propositions.text: Subjective fear issues arise but claimants did not establish harassment or discrimination amounting to persecution.
propositions.quote: Subjective fear issues are raised by his evidence and conduct and I do not find that the claimants established harassment or discrimination amounting to persecution

paragraphs.summary: Persecution requires repeated harm; PC fears individual but did not report; court finds no harassment amounting to persecution.

propositions.text: Convention refugee requires both subjective fear and objective well-foundedness of persecution fear.
propositions.quote: Both subjective and objective components are required to meet the definition

propositions.text: Lack of evidence on subjective fear alone suffices to fail claim.
propositions.quote: even a lack of evidence going to the subjective element of the claim is in itself sufficient for the claim to fail

paragraphs.summary: Convention refugee definition requires subjective and objective fear; lack of subjective evidence causes claim failure.

propositions.text: PC's multiple returns and failure to relocate suggest country shopping, not genuine refugee need.
propositions.quote: The PC's evidence presents a situation of multiple reavailments, and a failure to relocate away from a small town of alleged persecution over an extended period of time

propositions.text: Claimants' evidence reflects country shopping rather than genuine refugee need for protection.
propositions.quote: The evidence of the claimants is more reflective of a situation of country shopping, rather than of genuine refugees in need of international protection

paragraphs.summary: Court finds PC's conduct shows country shopping, not genuine refugee need.

propositions.text: Return to country may indicate lack of well-founded fear if conduct inconsistent with fear.
propositions.quote: Return to the country of nationality may indicate that a well-founded fear of persecution is lacking where the claimant's conduct is inconsistent with such fear

propositions.text: PC made multiple trips to Bosnia and Croatia; last return just before coming to Canada; wife gave similar evidence.
propositions.quote: The PC indicates multiple trips to Bosnia to visit friends and returns to Croatia; his last reavailment was just prior to coming to Canada. Similar evidence was provided by his wife

paragraphs.summary: Return trips may show lack of fear; PC and wife made multiple returns before coming to Canada.

propositions.text: Frequent returns to persecution area inconsistent with genuine subjective fear.
propositions.quote: The conduct of frequent returns to the country of alleged persecution is conduct inconsistent with a genuine subjective fear under the law

propositions.text: PC said he returned to visit mother despite persecution evidence.
propositions.quote: he stated that he had to go and visit his mother

propositions.text: Court finds it unreasonable that one fearing persecution would travel repeatedly to that area; adverse finding on subjective fear.
propositions.quote: I do not find it reasonable that one who genuinely fears persecution would be traveling and returning to the same area of persecution over an extended time. An adverse finding is drawn on the level of alleged subjective fear

paragraphs.summary: Court finds PC's frequent returns unreasonable and adverse to subjective fear claim.

propositions.text: Failure to relocate within Croatia raises subjective fear issues.
propositions.quote: Subjective fear issues also arise with the evidence on their failure to relocate in Croatia

propositions.text: PC said all towns have groups bothering each other, same in Serbia and Bosnia.
propositions.quote: the PC indicated that in each town, there are groups of people bothering each other. He stated that it is the same in Serbia and Bosnia also

propositions.text: Court finds it unreasonable for PC and family to remain in small town if in danger; they had access to larger cities and resources to relocate.
propositions.quote: I do not find it reasonable that the PC and his family would remain in their small town, if in such danger. They had access to larger, cosmopolitan cities where they could be away from their bothersome neighbours and be more anonymous. The claimants had the sophistication and resources to relocate to Canada, it would have been reasonable for them to try a more local solution prior to seeking international `protection. An adverse finding is drawn on their subjective fear

paragraphs.summary: Court finds failure to relocate locally unreasonable and adverse to subjective fear claim.

propositions.text: Claimants failed to establish past or future persecution on return to Croatia; PC alleges fear of individuals but problems were periodic.
propositions.quote: The claimants failed to establish that they will face any persecution on return to Croatia, or that they suffered past persecution in Croatia. While the PC alleges to fear specific individuals in his small town, he also indicates that the problems were periodic

paragraphs.summary: Court finds claimants failed to prove past or future persecution; problems were periodic.

propositions.text: Claimants did not establish subjective fear of genuine refugee; claim under s. 96 IRPA fails.
propositions.quote: The claimants did not establish with either their conduct or evidence, the level of subjective fear associated with a genuine refugee in need of international protection and as a result the claim under s. 96 of the IRPA fails

paragraphs.summary: Court concludes claimants failed to prove subjective fear; claim under s. 96 IRPA fails.

propositions.text: Claimants did not establish more than mere possibility of persecution on return; even if claim under s. 96 or 97(1) IRPA established, they failed to rebut presumption of state protection.
propositions.quote: While I do not find that the claimants established more than a mere possibility of persecution on return to Croatia, even had the claimants established a claim under s. 96 or 97(1) of the IRPA, they failed to rebut the presumption of state protection in Croatia today

paragraphs.summary: Court finds claimants failed to rebut presumption of state protection even if claim established.

propositions.text: Presumption that countries can protect citizens; international protection only if no other recourse.
propositions.quote: There is a presumption that countries are capable of protecting its citizens, and this underscores the principle that international protection comes into play only when a refugee claimant has no other recourse available

propositions.text: Claimant bears legal burden to rebut presumption of adequate state protection with clear and convincing evidence on balance of probabilities.
propositions.quote: the claimant bears the legal burden of rebutting the presumption that adequate state protection exists by adducing clear and convincing evidence which satisfies the Board on a balance of probabilities

paragraphs.summary: Law presumes countries protect citizens; claimant must rebut with clear, convincing evidence on balance of probabilities.

propositions.text: To rebut presumption, claimant must provide clear, convincing, reliable, probative evidence that state protection is inadequate on balance of probabilities.
propositions.quote: a claimant must provide "clear and convincing" evidence of the state's inability to protect its citizens. The evidence that state protection is inadequate must not only be reliable and probative, it must also satisfy the Board, on a balance of probabilities, that state protection is inadequate

paragraphs.summary: Claimant must provide clear, convincing, reliable evidence that state protection is inadequate on balance of probabilities.

propositions.text: High onus on claimant from democratic country to show all reasonable steps taken to seek protection considering context and interactions with authorities.
propositions.quote: the onus is high on a claimant coming from a democratic country. A claimant must show that they have taken all reasonable steps in the circumstances to seek protection, taking into account the context of the country of origin, the steps taken and the claimant's interactions with the authorities

paragraphs.summary: Claimant from democratic country must show all reasonable steps taken to seek protection.

propositions.text: State presumed capable of protection unless in complete breakdown; claimant must approach state if protection reasonably forthcoming or objectively reasonable to seek it.
propositions.quote: A state, unless in complete breakdown, is presumed to be capable of protecting its citizens, and international protection comes into play only when a refugee claimant cannot obtain protection domestically. A claimant is required to approach the state for protection if protection might reasonably be forthcoming or, alternatively, if it is objectively reasonable for the claimant to have sought protection

paragraphs.summary: State presumed capable unless breakdown; claimant must seek protection if reasonable to do so.

propositions.text: PC reported bullying of sons to police in 2005 and approached parents, causing family problems; only one police station in town where he reported.
propositions.quote: The PC indicates that in 2005 he reported to the police that his sons had been bullied. He took matters into his own hand and also approached the parents of one of the children, which led to problems for his family. The claimant identifies that there is just one police station in XXXX, and this is where he reported

paragraphs.summary: PC reported sons' bullying to police and parents in 2005; only one police station in town.

propositions.text: PC attended police with son after 2011 assault but could not identify attackers; police advised escorting son to school; PC unsatisfied; no police reports provided; no further reports or follow-up.
propositions.quote: The PC states that when his son was assaulted in 2011 in XXXX, while going to high school, he attended with his son at the police. He could not identify his attackers and the police indicated that if the PC was concerned about another event, he should escort his son to school. The PC was not satisfied. The PC has not provided any police reports in support of these events. Neither the PC, or his wife have reported any problems anywhere else, or followed up with the police where not satisfied with their action

paragraphs.summary: PC attended police after son's 2011 assault; no attacker ID; police advised escort; PC unsatisfied; no reports or follow-up.

propositions.text: PC fears specific individual who assaulted him but did not report due to fear of corrupt police.
propositions.quote: The PC indicates that he fears a specific individual, XXXX XXXX, who has assaulted him in the past; however he failed to report this to the police. When asked why he would fail to report a known assailant, the PC indicated that some of the police are corrupt and he feared reporting and having further problems

propositions.text: Adequacy of state protection cannot rest on claimant's subjective fear; claimant cannot rebut presumption by subjective reluctance to engage state.
propositions.quote: In refugee law the adequacy of state protection cannot rest on the subjective fear of the claimant; and a claimant cannot rebut the presumption of state protection in a functioning democracy by asserting only a subjective reluctance to engage the state

propositions.text: No failure of state protection where government not given opportunity to respond.
propositions.quote: there cannot be said to be a failure of state protection where a government has not been given an opportunity to respond

paragraphs.summary: PC fears assailant but did not report due to fear of corrupt police; law requires objective evidence and opportunity for state to respond.

propositions.text: Claimants did not provide clear and convincing evidence that state protection in Croatia is inadequate or that they exhausted all avenues before fleeing.
propositions.quote: I find that the claimants have not provided the requisite clear and convincing evidence that, on a balance of probabilities, state protection in Croatia is inadequate; or that they exhausted all avenues before fleeing to Canada

paragraphs.summary: Court finds claimants failed to prove inadequate state protection or exhaustion of all avenues before fleeing.

propositions.text: Croatia is a functioning electoral democracy with free and fair elections and structured government institutions.
propositions.quote: The objective evidence confirms that Croatia is functioning, and that there has been no breakdown of state institutions. Croatia is an electoral democracy. Both the 2009-2010 presidential poll and the 2007 parliamentary elections were deemed free and fair. The 153-member unicameral parliament (Sabor) is composed of 140 members from geographical districts, 8 of which represent ethnic minorities, and a variable number representing Croatians living abroad. All members are elected to four-year terms. The president of the republic, who serves as head of state, is elected by popular vote for a maximum of two five-year terms. The prime minister is appointed by the president but must be approved by the parliament. The national police have primary responsibility for national security; in times of disorder, the prime minister and the president may call upon the military to provide security. The intelligence service is under the authority of the prime minister and the president. An independent oversight board monitors intelligence service performance

paragraphs.summary: Court finds Croatia is a functioning democracy with free elections and established institutions.

propositions.text: The constitution guarantees freedoms of expression and the press, but reporters face political pressure and media influenced by advertisers.
propositions.quote: The constitution guarantees freedoms of expression and the press. While these rights are generally respected in practice, reporters remain vulnerable to political pressure, and journalists have alleged that the media are becoming increasingly beholden to the interests of powerful advertisers.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the constitution guarantees freedom of expression and press, but reporters face political pressure and media influenced by advertisers.

propositions.text: Freedom of religion, association, and assembly are constitutionally guaranteed; NGOs operate without interference; workers freely form unions with 64% unionization.
propositions.quote: Freedom of religion is guaranteed by the constitution. The constitution provides for freedoms of association and assembly. A variety of both international and domestic non-governmental organizations (NGOs) operate in Croatia without governmental interference or harassment. The constitution allows workers to form and join trade unions, and they do so freely. Approximately 64 percent of the workforce is unionized.

propositions.text: International Trade Union Confederation criticized 2009 Act for endangering collective bargaining; economic crisis weakened unions' participation in advisory council.
propositions.quote: Despite these freedoms, the International Trade Union Confederation criticized Croatia's 2009 Act on the Basis for Wages in Public Services for endangering the right to collective bargaining. The position of trade unions in the country has also been weakened by the recent global economic crisis, which has forced some trade union organizations to temporarily suspend their participation in the state's Economic and Social Council, an advisory body to the Croatian government which coordinates dialogue and harmonizes policies between employers, trade unions, and the government.

paragraphs.summary: The court notes constitutional guarantees for religion, association, assembly, NGOs, and unions, but union rights weakened by law and economic crisis.

propositions.text: Respect for minority rights in Croatia has improved but harassment and discrimination persist, especially against Serbs underrepresented in government.
propositions.quote: Respect for minority rights in Croatia has improved over the past decade, but various forms of harassment and discrimination persist. Ethnic minorities, particularly Serbs, remain under represented at several levels of government and in the civil administration.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds minority rights improved but harassment and Serb underrepresentation persist.

propositions.text: Returning Serbs still face harassment though declining; authorities protect minorities; constitutional protections against discrimination apply to all minorities.
propositions.quote: Returning Serbs are still harassed by the local population, although the frequency of such incidents is on the decline. Croatian authorities have taken steps to protect religious and ethnic minorities. Constitutional protections against discrimination apply to all minorities.

paragraphs.summary: The court states returning Serbs face less harassment; authorities protect minorities with constitutional anti-discrimination protections.

propositions.text: Minority groups guaranteed parliamentary seats and proportional public employment; National Minority Council funded; minorities entitled to education in own language.
propositions.quote: Minority groups are guaranteed seats in the Croatian parliament and in some areas are guaranteed proportional representation in public service employment. The National Minority Council receives significant government funding for minority cultural programs, and legislation entitles national minorities to primary and secondary education in their own language.

paragraphs.summary: The court notes minorities have guaranteed parliamentary seats, public employment, funded cultural programs, and education rights.

propositions.text: Government funds employers to hire minority workers; 2009 Anti-Discrimination Act makes ombudsman central equality promoter; claimants never approached ombudsman.
propositions.quote: The government also funds employers to hire minority workers. The 2009 Anti-Discrimination Act makes the ombudsman the central body for promoting equality. The Croatian ombudsman became the central body for promoting equality, with the passage of anti discrimination legislation in January, 2009. The claimants have never approached the Ombudsman for assistance.

propositions.text: PC aware of Ombudsman in Bosnia but not Croatia.
propositions.quote: The PC indicated in questioning that he was aware of the Ombudsman in Bosnia but not Croatia.

paragraphs.summary: The court states government funds minority hiring; ombudsman promotes equality; claimants never sought ombudsman help; PC unaware of Croatian ombudsman.

propositions.text: UN Human Rights Council reports equality principle enshrined; hate crimes recognized; anti-discrimination laws and plans exist; hate crime monitoring established.
propositions.quote: It is noted in the United Nations, Human Rights Council Report that: "The principle of equality was enshrined in the Constitution and enjoyed special legal protection, and the Criminal Code recognized the concept of hate crimes. The 2008 Antidiscrimination Act and the National Plan for Combating Discrimination (2008-2013) were other instruments to counter discrimination. In 2010, Croatia had established a new Working Group to monitor hate crimes at the national level.

propositions.text: Efforts to combat discrimination against minorities and LGBT persons; politicians promote tolerance; investigations of hate crimes increasing.
propositions.quote: Special efforts were devoted to combating discrimination against minorities, including the Serb and the Roma minorities and lesbian, gay, bisexual and transgender persons. Special attention was being paid both to awareness-raising activities and the strengthening of institutional capacity. Politicians were increasingly spreading the message of tolerance and reconciliation. Recent trends had indicated an increase in the investigation of hate crimes.

propositions.text: Criminal acts against journalists treated seriously; assaults led to criminal charges and first-instance judgments.
propositions.quote: Criminal acts directed against journalists, particularly attacks on their physical integrity, were treated with the utmost seriousness and tended to be characterized as grave crimes under the Criminal Code. A number of assaults against journalists had resulted in criminal charges, as recently demonstrated through the first-instance judgement in respect of the killings of media professionals Pukanic and Franjic.

paragraphs.summary: UN report notes constitutional equality, hate crime laws, anti-discrimination efforts, increased hate crime investigations, and serious treatment of journalist assaults.

propositions.text: Adequate state protection requires effective programs; government actions have concrete results including improved police investigations and minority political representation.
propositions.quote: For there to be adequate state protection, there needs to be signs of effectiveness of programs as well. The government's actions have had concrete results. A 2008 European Union progress report notes that police investigations of ethnically-motivated incidents have improved, although too few cases end in prosecutions. Adequate political representation of minorities has been achieved in some local and regional assemblies.

propositions.text: Ethnically-motivated crime perpetrators arrested, charged, convicted; minority situation improved overall.
propositions.quote: In other cases, individuals who committed ethnically-motivated crimes were arrested, charged, and convicted and the situation of minorities in general has improved.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds state protection effective with improved police investigations, minority political representation, and convictions for ethnic crimes.

propositions.text: Croatia does not provide perfect protection; minorities still face harassment and discrimination.
propositions.quote: None of this means that Croatia provides perfect protection to its citizens, including ethnic and religious minorities. Members of minorities are still confronted with harassment and discrimination.

propositions.text: Some sources allege slow or ineffective government response to discrimination and violence; investigations and prosecutions criticized as slow.
propositions.quote: Some sources allege slow or ineffective reaction by the authorities to allegations of discrimination or violence against minorities, and investigative and prosecutorial actions have been criticized as slow.

propositions.text: Government does not always observe law requiring proportional minority representation in public employment.
propositions.quote: The government does not always observe the law requiring proportional minority representation in public service employment.

paragraphs.summary: The court acknowledges imperfect protection with ongoing harassment, slow government response, and inconsistent minority employment representation.

propositions.text: UN Human Rights Council notes Croatia developed advanced human rights protection system meeting international standards, important for EU membership.
propositions.quote: Lastly, it is noted by the United Nations Human Rights Council report that Croatia has developed an advanced human rights protection system which is based on meeting international human rights standards. This is critical as Croatia has joined the European Union.

paragraphs.summary: UN report notes Croatia's advanced human rights system meeting international standards, important for EU membership.

propositions.text: Objective evidence on state protection is mixed and does not clearly rebut presumption of state protection.
propositions.quote: The objective evidence regarding state protection for individuals such as the claimants is mixed, and as such, is not a clear and convincing rebuttal of the presumption of state protection, as required.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds mixed evidence does not clearly rebut presumption of state protection.

propositions.text: Claimants must provide clear and convincing evidence to rebut presumption of state protection; panel does not have to prove it.
propositions.quote: It is not for the panel to set out clear and convincing evidence to support the presumption of state protection, it is for the claimants to provide such evidence to rebut the presumption.

propositions.text: Neither mixed objective evidence nor claimants' evidence clearly and convincingly rebuts state protection presumption.
propositions.quote: Neither the mixed objective evidence nor the claimants' own evidence is a clear and convincing rebuttal of state protection.

paragraphs.summary: The court states claimants must rebut presumption of state protection with clear evidence; neither evidence suffices here.

propositions.text: Panel finds adequate state protection available to claimants; they are not entitled to Canada's surrogate protection.
propositions.quote: The panel finds that adequate state protection is available to the claimants in their country, and as such, they are not entitled to or in need of Canada's surrogate protection.

paragraphs.summary: The court concludes claimants have adequate state protection and are not entitled to Canada's surrogate protection.

propositions.text: Claimants have not established well-founded fear of persecution and failed to rebut presumption of state protection.
propositions.quote: The claimants have not established a well founded fear of persecution, with their evidence or conduct, and have failed to rebut the presumption of state protection.

paragraphs.summary: The court concludes claimants failed to establish fear of persecution and rebut presumption of state protection.
